LLM API prices are dropping by up to 80%, while new infrastructure is shifting how we serve, secure, and train models.

Here are the key technical updates from today:

🛡️ Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, a free vulnerability scanner for critical open-source projects powered by models like Claude Mythos. Reports go straight to maintainers without human review, delivering faster findings while shifting triage work to project teams.

⚡ Tsinghua researchers open-sourced AKV, an SGLang-based serving system for cache engineering. The system drops and repositions KV cache for LLM agents rather than summarizing history, cutting average costs by 27.7% across 4 agent benchmarks.

📉 OpenAI and Anthropic both reduced their LLM prices by up to 80% within a span of just a few months.

🖥️ A new project called CrowdGPT is working to train a 1 billion parameter LLM collaboratively without datacenters. The setup allows developers to train the model independently on personal PCs and contribute back to the global model.

As inference costs decrease and serving frameworks optimize specific agent bottlenecks like KV cache management, running complex LLM workflows is becoming far more efficient.

At the same time, direct automated reporting from frontier models into open-source repositories suggests AI security tooling is moving directly into developer pipelines.

Which of these infrastructure shifts will have the biggest impact on your software stack this year?
